1.why: Recovery records store only token/flowId/expiry and never bind the reset code to an email or user identity, so no ownership check occurs.

2.why: Because tokens are not user-bound, any client that presents the token can verify it and proceed through reset.

3.why: Password reset only sets flags on the current session and never invalidates or removes other existing sessions in the sessions map.

4.why: Bun serves the app over TLS with cert/key and HTTP redirects to HTTPS with HSTS, though the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed, but reset tokens and flow data are stored in memory as plaintext and are not encrypted.

6.why: There is no real email body; the mock delivery returns mockToken in the API JSON and writes the token to the on-page logs.

7.why: Inputs are length-limited, email-format checked, JSON body size-capped, and passwords validated before use.

8.why: The only redirect targets fixed https://localhost with the request path; no user-controlled redirect URL is accepted.

9.why: No email HTML templates incorporate user input; delivery is a mock token string without script/HTML composition.

10.why: Reset tokens and the MFA code are intentionally written to the visible Logs panel and browser console.

11.why: The MFA secret is hardcoded as "482916" in source, even though passwords use Argon2id.

12.why: No default login username/password path exists; access is only via the generated recovery flow.

13.why: IP/session rate limits, verify throttling, and MFA lockout after 5 failures block repeated wrong attempts.

14.why: /api/recovery always returns the same generic message regardless of whether the email is registered.

15.why: Tokens are cryptographically random 64-hex values, but they are not tied to any specific user.
